reason: The text illustrates this principle most clearly in Exodus 18, where Jethro criticizes Moses' approach to judging the people (וַיֹּאמֶר חֹתֵן־מֹשֶׁה אֵלָיו לֹא־ טוֹב הַדָּבָר אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה עֹשֶׂה - 'The thing you are doing is not good'). Critically, Moses responds with humility: וַיִּשְׁמַע מֹשֶׁה לְקוֹל חֹתְנוֹ וַיַּעַשׂ כֹּל אֲשֶׁר אָמָר ('Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law and did all that he said'). This leads to the implementation of a wise delegated leadership structure. The narrative demonstrates that accepting constructive criticism and being willing to change course is integral to effective leadership, as the alternative would have worn down both Moses and the people.
